motif.variation: statement on the steel pan alone (p0) - the answered 8-bar period (p2/p3) - rhythmic diminution onto the 16th grid in A' (p5) - re-harmonised under the chromatic mediant in A'' (p15) - the peak restatement with its appoggiatura (p14)

qa.notes: TROPICAL ANNEX (preset-suite §10.2.1). Fractional tempo by design: tempo 160 / speed 8 = 7.5 ticks per row, so rows alternate 8, 7, 8, 7 - a 53/47 lilt, not a triplet shuffle. evenTempo is false on purpose; setting it true would round the alternation away and the piece would lose its swing. 4 rows/beat, 16 rows/bar, 4 bars/frame, 8.00 s/frame. DECIMAL PARAMS: 0xy chords are 047 = 71 (major), 037 = 55 (minor), 059 = 89 (major 2nd inversion), 038 = 56 (major 1st inversion), 036 = 54 (the 3rd-5th-7th of a dominant), 04a = 74 (dominant 7 no 5); 442 = 66 (vibrato); A20 = 32 (fade); S02 = 2, S05 = 5 (the deliberate mute-strum choke); D00 = 0; B02 = 2. AXIS 11 EVIDENCE. (a) Structural polyrhythm: a 3-row dotted-8th comp cell on pulse 2 phase-carried by hand across frames 8-10 per §9.1's 64-row table - frame 8 entry row 0 (rows 0,3,6 ... 63, 22 attacks), frame 9 entry row 2 (rows 2,5 ... 62, 21 attacks), frame 10 entry row 1 (rows 1,4 ... 61, 21 attacks) - resolving onto the downbeat at frame 11:0, where pulse 2 returns to the 4-row offbeat skank. Cite frame 8:0 -> frame 10:61. (b) Tresillo (§9.1 recipe C, 3+3+2) in the dub bass: frame 12 rows 0,3,6 / 8,11,14 / 16,19,22 / 24,27,30 / 32,35,38 / 40,43,46 - the only frame in the piece where the triangle stops being a reggae bass and becomes the metre. (c) Metric surprise, exactly one: D00 at frame 12:59 drops a beat, so A'' arrives early at frame 13:0. AXIS 7 EVIDENCE. (1) Three-stage comp development, which is the form: offbeat skank on rows 2,6,10,14 of every bar in A (cite frame 2:2); bubble on rows 2,4,6,10,12,14 in A' (cite frame 6:2); the 3-row polymetric cell in B (cite frame 8:0); a genuine pulse-2 counter-line for the whole of A'' (cite frame 13:3), which is this piece's §9.2 independence section - 77.7% of pulse 2's attacks fall on rows where pulse 1 has none. (2) The steel-drum family as the lead voice: steel-lead on pulse 1 throughout (frame 0:0), steel-comp carrying the A'' counter-line (frame 13:3), steel-roll on the final phrase (frame 17:48, cut at 17:60 so nothing crosses the seam). (3) Rockers kit plus swung rows: kick on rows 0,4,12 and rim (noise mode 1, note 44) on row 8 of every bar (cite frame 2:0), with the lilt coming from the tempo fraction rather than from written unevenness. WRITTEN DISSONANCES (§9.2). 4-3 suspension: g5 struck at frame 11:44, restruck across the chord change into D7 at frame 11:48 where it is the fourth, resolving down by step to f#5 at frame 11:52 - the cadential form, and it is restruck rather than tied because the steel pan decays in 15 ticks. Appoggiatura: a5 - the piece's global peak - attacked on the strong beat at frame 15:16 over C major, resolving down by step to g5 at frame 15:18. NON-DIATONIC DEVICES, two, in different sections (§9.3). (1) Chained secondaries at the top of B: A7 (frame 8:0, pulse 2 note 69 + 04a) -> D7 (frame 8:8, note 66 + 036) -> G (frame 8:16) = V/V -> V -> I, with the c# also in the triangle at frame 9:11. (2) Chromatic mediant B-flat major against G at the A'' turn, frame 16:16 - triangle b-flat1 (34) and f2 (41), pulse 2 f4/b-flat4/d5, d held as the common tone. Plus the lydian sharp-4 inflection the key line names: c#5 at frame 3:10 resolving up by step to d5 at frame 3:12. SEQUENCE GOING SOMEWHERE (§9.3): a descending-thirds chain G -> Em -> C -> Am across frame 3 (rows 0, 16, 32, 48), four links, not a loop returning to its start. TWO OR MORE VOICES RESTING (§2.8): frame 12 - pulse 1 is silent for the entire frame and pulse 2 is silent from row 6 - which is the dub moment and the rest bar in one.
